subject: Acme — RAG eval follow-up & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme — RAG eval follow-up & recommended next steps

Hi Elena —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking us through the search UX and the 2 customer support flows you care most about (KB retrieval for symptom resolution, and multi-doc summarization for executive briefs). Quick recap + recommended next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Primary goals: reduce hallucinations on KB answers, improve grounding rate on 1-click suggested replies, and keep 99th-pctl latency <= 800ms for single-turn lookups.
- Data: ~120k docs, mix of short KB articles and longer playbooks; we discussed redaction/PII constraints.

Redwood recommendations (high-level):
1) Models: evaluate Redwood-4-13B for quality-first flows and Redwood-3-7B (quantized) for latency-sensitive paths. Use Redwood-Embed-1 for dense retrieval.
2) Retrieval & reranking: start with chunk_size=512 tokens, chunk_overlap=64, initial dense retrieval top_k=100 + cross-encoder reranker re-rank top 10.
3) Eval metrics: grounding@1 (precision of first answer being grounded), hallucination_rate (manual + automated checks), and latency P99.

Attached: acme_rag_eval_results.pdf (summary of initial offline eval), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (your sample prompts + annotations), redwood_model_recommendations.md (benchmarks & tradeoffs). Also adding HubSpot link and a Drive folder with raw evaluation outputs.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm which two flows to prioritize for the live eval (I suggested KB lookup + suggested reply).
- We run a short gated eval (500 prompts — your prompt set) with the above retrieval/rerank settings and share a report in 3 business days.
- Optional: schedule a 30-min tech sync (Vivek + Neha) to lock retrieval tuning and metadata filters.

Are you available for a 30-min technical sync on Tue 11/10 or Wed 11/11? We can also proceed asynchronously if you prefer.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: acme_rag_eval_results.pdf; prompt_set_v1.jsonl; redwood_model_recommendations.md

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme — RAG eval follow-up & recommended next steps

Elena — quick answers + some concrete numbers so you can evaluate tradeoffs.

Latency / model guidance:
- Redwood-4-13B (FP16) on Dedicated (A100-like) typically P95 ~ 200-350ms generation for short completions (<= 150 tokens), P99 ~ 500-900ms depending on batching and KV-cache warm. Achievable for single-turn KB lookups with tuned batching/pinning.
- Redwood-3-7B (int8/quantized) P95 ~ 80-150ms, P99 ~ 200-350ms — good fit for latency SLOs but quality gap vs 13B on multi-hop summarization.

Reranker strategy:
- Recommendation: hybrid approach. Use dense retrieval (Redwood-Embed-1) to retrieve top_k=100, then a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (re-rank-XL-v1) to re-rank top 10 on the critical path. Cache reranker outputs for repeat queries to reduce cost.
- Cost example (gated eval): reranker adds ~0.2-0.5 USD per query at our standard pricing depending on sequence lengths; we can minimize cost by reranking only when the dense-sim score is below a threshold.

Security / residency:
- Redwood Private or Dedicated (VPC) supports KMS for envelope encryption; audits (SOC 2) available. For initial eval we can set up a transient managed index with enterprise KMS and strict TTLs.

Eval plan & timeline:
- Day 0: confirm prompt set + flows (you)
- Day 1-2: offline run (500 prompts) + metrics (grounding@1, hallucination_rate, P99 latency)
- Day 3: share report + recommended tuning (chunk size, top_k, reranker threshold)

Links: benchmark snapshot: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/rag/2026-acme-report
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If this looks reasonable I'll sync with Vivek to prepare a short eval config and the reranker cache policy.

-Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme — RAG eval follow-up & recommended next steps (technical notes)

Elena — adding technical specifics on the eval harness and grounding metrics so expectations are aligned.

Eval harness/config (proposed defaults):
- Retrieval: FAISS index (IVF-PQ) with metadata filtering by product_line and doc_type. Chunking: 512 tokens, overlap 64. Use embedding model Redwood-Embed-1, normalize embeddings.
- Retrieval top_k: 100 (dense) -> reranker top_k: 10. Reranker model: re-rank-XL-v1 (cross-encoder). Thresholding: only rerank when densest score < 0.75 to reduce cost.
- Grounding metrics:
  * Grounding@1: percent where the top answer cites at least one doc span that contains the golden answer or supporting evidence.
  * Hallucination rate: fraction of answers flagged by automated heuristics + human spot checks.
  * Attribution precision: fraction of cited spans that are semantically relevant (sampled).

Evaluation notes:
- For KB lookups, prioritize high precision for top-1; for summarization flows prioritize coherence and multi-doc grounding.
- Suggest adding a small human annotation pass (50 samples) to calibrate automated heuristics for hallucination detection.

Security note: we can provision a transient, encrypted index with short TTL for the eval. If you need to bring-your-own-key we support AWS KMS + HSM-based key wrapping.

I can prepare the eval config (YAML) and a short script to run locally or in your VPC. Would you like the config as a gist in Drive or we push to your repo?

—Vivek
Senior ML Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
